stables.backstory: Part man, part machine, all paperwork. One unit, one sidearm, and an upgrade budget signed off by the board. The precinct does not field a team — it does not need one.

stables.backstory: It will not stop. It will not yield. Skynet sends a single unit back into every season and spends everything it has on making that unit harder to kill.

Liquid-metal figure with blade arms

stables.backstory: Two pilots, one mind, a lot of steel. The Corps fights in pairs because that is the only way it knows how — linked, shoulder to shoulder, holding the line one tag-team bout at a time.

stables.backstory: Built to help, upgraded to fight. Light Labs sends its two brothers into the tag-team circuit with a simple philosophy: learn from every opponent, charge the shot, and never leave a teammate behind.

stables.backstory: Peace through tyranny, and tyranny through superior firepower. The Armada fields three of its most notorious commanders as one 3v3 unit and lets the rest of the arena argue about who is really in charge.

stables.backstory: A battered carrier, a green crew and three prototypes nobody planned to send into combat. White Base learns on the job: upgrade what survives, refit what does not, and keep the formation tight.

stables.backstory: Planet Express treats the arena as a side business. The merchandise sells, the streams pay, and the robots are mostly there to keep the cameras rolling. Profit first; glory if it is cheap.

stables.backstory: Somewhere between a sport and a spectacle. The league sells tickets, streams every bout and puts the takings back into the ring. Its fighters range from scrapped-together sparring bots to polished champions, and the crowd loves an underdog.

stables.backstory: Disciplined, adaptable and stubbornly decent. The Autobots bring a little of everything to the arena — a leader, a scout, a heavy and a medic — and grow carefully, one well-equipped robot at a time.
